items.value: Statement I is correct (dust is more concentrated in subtropical and temperate regions), but Statement II is not: those regions have MORE dry winds, not less
items.reasoning: The higher concentration of dust particles in subtropical and temperate latitudes is a standard fact, and the stated cause is the prevalence of DRY winds there, which lift and carry dust; equatorial regions have heavy rainfall that washes dust out and polar regions have snow cover and little loose surface material. Statement II inverts the causal fact by saying these areas have 'less dry winds', so it is incorrect while Statement I stands.

items.value: Both statements are correct, and the January warmth of Northern Hemisphere oceans relative to land is exactly why isotherms bend poleward over oceans and equatorward over land
items.reasoning: In January the Northern Hemisphere is in winter: land loses heat rapidly because of its low specific heat, while the oceans, aided by warm currents such as the Gulf Stream and North Atlantic Drift, stay relatively warm. A given temperature value is therefore found further north over the ocean and further south over the continent, which is precisely the equatorward-over-land, poleward-over-sea bending described in Statement I. So Statement II is not merely also true, it is the explanation of Statement I.

items.value: Only Statement II is correct (chalk is porous and absorbs water) and it explains Statement I; Statement III is wrong because clay IS porous
items.reasoning: Clay has very high porosity, often 40 to 60 per cent by volume, but its pores are microscopic and poorly connected, so water cannot move through it; that is why clay is impermeable despite being porous. Statement III therefore fails, which rules out options A and B. Statement II is correct and accounts for chalk being permeable, so option D also fails and only C survives. Porosity and permeability are different properties, and this item turns entirely on that distinction.

items.value: All three statements are correct: the atmosphere keeps the surface above freezing, trapped heat maintains the average temperature, and gases like carbon dioxide are strong absorbers of radiation
items.reasoning: Statements II and III are the textbook description of the greenhouse effect and are plainly correct. Statement I is the standard companion claim: without atmospheric absorption the Earth's equilibrium temperature would be about -18 degrees Celsius, well below freezing. The word 'everywhere' is a slight overstatement, since an airless sunlit surface would in fact be hot like the Moon's dayside, but the three statements read as one passage on the greenhouse effect and the intended reading is that all are correct.

items.value: Both statements about the Rashtriya Gokul Mission are correct
items.reasoning: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission was launched in December 2014 for the development and conservation of indigenous bovine breeds, and its stated aim is to promote indigenous cattle and buffalo rearing and conservation in a scientific and holistic manner, so Statement II is correct. The scheme's own rationale explicitly notes that most low-producing indigenous animals are held by small and marginal farmers and landless labourers, making the mission an instrument of rural upliftment, so Statement I is correct too.

items.value: Both Statements II and III are correct, but only the conversion of limestone into lime explains the cement industry's large carbon emissions
items.reasoning: Cement is widely estimated to account for about 7 to 8 per cent of global carbon dioxide emissions, so Statement I is correct, and the raw meal for cement genuinely is limestone blended with silica-bearing clay or shale, so Statement II is correct. But merely mixing clay with limestone releases no carbon dioxide. The emissions come from calcination, where calcium carbonate breaks down into lime and carbon dioxide, which is Statement III. Hence both are correct but only III is the explanation.

items.value: Only Statement III is correct and it explains India's abstention; Statement II is wrong because the COP28 Declaration on Climate and Health is voluntary, not binding
items.reasoning: The COP28 UAE Declaration on Climate and Health, endorsed by well over a hundred countries, is a political and non-binding declaration, so Statement II is false and options A and B are ruled out. India did not sign it, and the concern reported was that mandated decarbonisation of the health sector would constrain the cooling and energy use that hospitals in a hot country need, weakening health-system resilience, which is Statement III. Since one of the two is correct and does explain Statement I, option C follows and D is ruled out.

items.value: Both Statements II and III are correct, but only the equatorward redistribution of meltwater explains the shift in the Earth's rotation and axis
items.reasoning: Statement III is the recognised mechanism: as polar ice melts, mass moves from the poles towards lower latitudes, increasing the Earth's moment of inertia, slowing its rotation and displacing the rotational pole. Statement II is a true statement in itself, since solar flares and coronal mass ejections do deposit enormous energy in the outer atmosphere, but that energy affects the ionosphere, satellites and power grids, not the planet's mass distribution, so it cannot explain a shift in the axis. Both correct, only one explanatory, hence B rather than A or C.

items.value: Both Statements II and III are correct and both explain why Article 6 is so prominent: it covers carbon markets and also non-market cooperative approaches
items.reasoning: Article 6 of the Paris Agreement has two market limbs, 6.2 cooperative approaches using internationally transferred mitigation outcomes and 6.4 the centralised crediting mechanism, so Statement II is correct. It also has Article 6.8, a framework for non-market approaches through which countries cooperate without trading credits, so Statement III is correct. Both limbs are written in the Agreement as serving sustainable development, and it is exactly this combined market-plus-non-market scope that makes Article 6 a recurring subject of global climate and sustainable-development negotiation, so both explain Statement I.

items.value: The Asian Development Bank launched the Nature Solutions Finance Hub for Asia and the Pacific
items.reasoning: The Nature Solutions Finance Hub for Asia and the Pacific was announced by the Asian Development Bank at COP28 in Dubai, to develop and finance nature-positive projects and mobilise capital for natural capital in the region. Its mandate is region-specific to Asia and the Pacific, which is ADB's remit; the AIIB is an infrastructure investment bank, the NDB is the BRICS bank and the IBRD is the World Bank's main lending arm, none of which launched this hub.

items.value: All three uses of Direct Air Capture are correct: sequestration, feedstock for plastics and food processing, and a carbon source for synthetic aviation fuel
items.reasoning: Direct Air Capture removes carbon dioxide from ambient air, and when the captured gas is injected into geological storage the process is a form of carbon sequestration, so Statement I is correct. Captured carbon dioxide is also a commercial feedstock, used in polymer and plastic manufacture and in food and beverage processing such as carbonation and chilling, so Statement II is correct. And in aviation it supplies the carbon that is combined with green hydrogen to synthesise low-carbon e-fuels, so Statement III is correct.

items.value: Statements II and III are correct; the Peacock tarantula is an arachnid, not an omnivorous crustacean
items.reasoning: Statement I is wrong twice over: the Gooty or Peacock tarantula, Poecilotheria metallica, is a spider and therefore an arachnid, not a crustacean, and it is a carnivorous predator on insects rather than an omnivore. Its wild population is confined to a very small patch of reserve forest in the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh, which makes Statement II correct and is why it is listed as Critically Endangered. Poecilotheria species are tree-dwelling, sheltering in holes in tall trees, so Statement III is correct as well.

items.value: Statements II and III are correct; India's per capita carbon dioxide emission is around 2 tonnes, far above the 0.5 tonne figure claimed in Statement I
items.reasoning: India's carbon dioxide emissions per person are roughly 1.9 to 2.0 tonnes a year, low by world standards but four times the under-0.5-tonne figure in Statement I, so Statement I is incorrect. India is the second-largest emitter from fuel combustion in the Asia-Pacific region after China, so Statement II is correct. Electricity and heat generation, dominated by coal-fired power, is by a wide margin India's single largest emitting sector at roughly half of national emissions, so Statement III is correct.

items.value: Only three pairs match: cassava as a woody shrub, ginger as a herb with a pseudostem, and Malabar spinach as a herbaceous climber; mint and papaya are wrongly described
items.reasoning: Cassava, Manihot esculenta, is correctly described as a woody perennial shrub; ginger's aerial shoot is a pseudostem formed by tightly rolled leaf sheaths on a herbaceous perennial; and Malabar spinach, Basella alba, is a succulent herbaceous climbing vine. Mint is a perennial HERB, not an annual shrub, so pair IV fails. Papaya has a single unbranched, soft, hollow, non-woody stem and is described as a small tree or a giant herb rather than a woody shrub, which is multi-stemmed and branched from the base, so pair V fails. Three correct pairs.

items.value: Only Statement II is correct: marine phytoplankton and photosynthetic bacteria supply about half the world's oxygen
items.reasoning: Statement I is the reverse of the truth, since ocean phytoplankton, not rainforests, are the larger oxygen source, and mature rainforests consume through respiration and decay nearly as much oxygen as they produce. Statement II is the standard figure of about 50 per cent or more from marine photosynthesis, and is correct. Statement III is badly wrong on magnitude: air is about 21 per cent oxygen, around 210,000 parts per million, whereas well-oxygenated water holds only 8 to 10 milligrams per litre, so water contains far less oxygen than air, not several times more.

items.value: All three are alternative powertrain vehicles
items.reasoning: Alternative powertrain simply means any drivetrain other than the conventional internal combustion engine running on petrol or diesel. Full battery electric vehicles run on stored electricity, hydrogen fuel cell vehicles generate electricity onboard from hydrogen, and fuel cell-electric hybrids combine a fuel cell with a battery. All three replace the conventional engine, so all three qualify.

items.value: None of the three statements is correct, because each says ALL types of UAV can do something that fixed-wing UAVs cannot
items.reasoning: Each statement is universal, and a single class of UAV defeats all three. Fixed-wing UAVs need a runway, a catapult or a net or parachute recovery, so they cannot all land vertically, defeating Statement I. Fixed-wing aircraft must maintain forward airspeed to generate lift and so cannot hover, defeating Statement II. And UAVs are powered by internal combustion and turbine engines, hydrogen fuel cells and solar cells as well as batteries, defeating Statement III. Hence none.

items.value: Three of them, cobalt, lithium and nickel, make up battery cathodes; graphite is the anode material
items.reasoning: The cathode of a typical electric-vehicle lithium-ion cell is a lithium metal oxide such as nickel-manganese-cobalt or nickel-cobalt-aluminium oxide, so lithium, nickel and cobalt are all cathode constituents. Graphite is the standard ANODE material, into whose layers lithium ions intercalate on charging, and it is not part of the cathode. So exactly three of the four listed elements are cathode materials.

items.value: All three contain plastic
items.reasoning: Cigarette filters are made of cellulose acetate, a plastic, which is why discarded butts are among the most common plastic litter items in the world. Modern eyeglass lenses are predominantly plastic, such as CR-39 or polycarbonate, having largely replaced glass. Car tyres are built from synthetic rubber, a petroleum-derived polymer, and tyre wear is one of the largest single sources of microplastic pollution. So all three contain plastic.

items.value: Coal gasification can contribute to the production of all three: ethanol, nitroglycerine and urea
items.reasoning: Coal gasification yields syngas, a mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen. Ethanol is made from syngas directly or through methanol, and urea is made from gasification-derived ammonia combined with carbon dioxide, so those two are clear. Nitroglycerine is the doubtful one: its carbon skeleton is glycerol, which does not come from coal, but the nitric acid that nitrates it is made from ammonia, which coal gasification supplies, and Indian coal gasification literature lists nitrogenous explosives among downstream products. On the permissive wording 'can be used in the production of', all three qualify, but a reading that requires coal to supply the carbon backbone would give only two, so this item is genuinely arguable between C and B.

items.value: CL-20, HMX and LLM-105 are all high explosives used in military weapons
items.reasoning: HMX, or octogen, is a long-established military high explosive; CL-20, hexanitrohexaazaisowurtzitane, is among the most powerful non-nuclear explosives known; and LLM-105 is an insensitive high explosive developed for munitions that must survive shock and heat without detonating. Their shared identity is that they are energetic nitro compounds used as explosives. Some of them do also appear in solid rocket propellant formulations, which is what options C and D play on, but that is a secondary application, not the common characteristic.

items.value: Statements I and III are correct; the Majorana 1 chip is Microsoft's, not Amazon Web Services'
items.reasoning: Majorana 1 is Microsoft's topological quantum processor, announced in February 2025 and built on a topoconductor intended to host Majorana zero modes for error-resistant qubits, so Statement I is correct and Statement II, which credits Amazon Web Services, is wrong. Deep learning, which uses multi-layered neural networks, is a subset of machine learning, which is itself a subset of artificial intelligence, so Statement III is correct.

items.value: All three statements on monoclonal antibodies are correct
items.reasoning: Monoclonal antibodies are laboratory-produced protein molecules, so Statement I is correct. They are engineered to bind one specific antigen, and through that binding they mimic, restore or enhance the immune system's attack on the target, so Statement II is correct as a description of how they act immunologically. Monoclonal antibodies are indeed used against viral infections, and the m102.4 antibody has been deployed on compassionate grounds against Nipah virus in India, so Statement III is correct. Statement II is the only debatable one, since many monoclonals work by blocking rather than stimulating, but the standard description supports it.

items.value: None of the three statements is correct; each denies something viruses demonstrably do
items.reasoning: Seawater is the most virus-rich environment on Earth, holding on the order of ten million virus particles per millilitre, so Statement I is false. Bacteriophages are viruses whose hosts are bacteria and they are the most abundant biological entities known, so Statement II is false. And viruses routinely hijack host transcription, shutting down host genes and redirecting the cell's machinery to make viral products, so Statement III is false. All three are false, hence none.

items.value: Both Statements II and III are correct and both explain Statement I: the large adsorbing surface makes activated carbon effective, and its easy synthesis from waste makes it attractive
items.reasoning: Statement I makes a two-part claim, that activated carbon is both a GOOD and an ATTRACTIVE tool. Statement II supplies the first half, since a surface area running to hundreds or over a thousand square metres per gram gives it a strong capacity to adsorb heavy metals and organic pollutants. Statement III supplies the second half, since activated carbon can be prepared cheaply from carbon-rich waste such as coconut shell, rice husk and other agricultural residues, which is exactly what makes it economically attractive as well as effective. Both statements are correct and each explains one half of Statement I.
